questions.question: What is the purpose of using a Broadcast block in PicToBlox?
options: To make a sprite speak for 5 seconds
To send a secret signal so that multiple sprites and scripts can communicate and act together
To delete all variables from memory
To change the volume of the sound effects
questions.explanation: Spot on! Staging a broadcast sends a message across the entire program. Any sprite listening for that specific broadcast will react instantly.

questions.question: Which block is used as a starting hat block that triggers code when another sprite sends a message?
questions.explanation: Correct! 'when I receive' is the starting block that activates once a corresponding broadcast signal is sent.

questions.question: Which colored block drawer contains the 'pick random' block used to generate surprise numbers in PicToBlox?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'pick random' block belongs to the green Operators drawer, which handles math and comparison logic.

questions.question: If you want an enemy bug sprite in a frog game to constantly appear at random heights on the screen, which block combination is correct?
questions.explanation: Great! Putting a 'pick random' block inside a 'set y' or 'change y' block generates a randomized height for our enemy sprites.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to broadcast a message named 'start_game'.
questions.explanation: Perfect! The broadcast block allows different parts of your code and different sprites to coordinate and start actions together.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to set the sprite's X position to a random number between -100 and 100.
questions.task_hint: Write: set x to pick random -100 to 100
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Placing 'pick random' inside coordinates blocks allows you to place enemies or objects in random horizontal spots.
